title: I Just Used AI to File My Equal Opportunity Complaint Against UnitedHealth Group!
subtitle: I could not be more excited to see the future of Compliance made real, days after I predicted it.
text:
So while ago, I wrote a really long and really complicated column about UnitedHealth Group.

I applied for a behavioral medical director job, and then they asked me about my disability status, and then they declined me for the job.

Now, the conceit of the article, buried in the footnotes, was that my constant shit posting about United and their abrupt and automated dismissal of me, especially in the context of evaluating my disability status was the basis for an employment law claim. And now, dear readers, after writing another article, just this week about how AI was going to automate Compliance … Well, I have news for you, AI just automated Compliance. I took the legal argument from the footnotes of my article about united, dropped it into and AI tool. It’s called: DoNotPay, and now my esoteric legal theory is a filing with the equal employment opportunity commission.

I can’t believe how fast the future got here. I wrote the article about automating Compliance on the 27th, and before the end of the goddamn month, I filed the first legal complaint.

This is going to be awesome. I am so excited to tell you about this tomorrow. is the one who pointed it out in the first place! This is gonna be a blast.

I’m not saying this wins, I’m just saying it’s the best proof of concept of the year. Hospital price transparency, IRS regulation 501r Compliance, discrimination and mental health parity violations, late payment, this is just my dream come true.

—O. Scott Muir, M.D.
